clue.text: Child holds vestment for Joan of Arc's opponent

indicators.note: the child word contains, or holds, the vestment word in its middle

parts.note: a tot is a small child
an alb is a white linen vestment worn by a priest

explanation.surface: A youngster grasps a priest's robe, oddly described as an enemy of the Maid of Orleans.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Talbot is the English commander who fights Joan la Pucelle in Shakespeare's Henry VI Part 1.
explanation.definitionFit: John Talbot was the English general who opposed the French heroine in the Hundred Years War and in Shakespeare's history play.

clue.text: A chapter note pointed up for the scholarly community

parts.note: A is a musical note

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word for pointed is written bottom to top

parts.note: to aim is to point, so aimed means pointed

explanation.surface: A chapter has a note pointed upwards, for scholars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns AIMED into DEMIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Academia is the world of universities and scholars.

clue.text: Hero's 'defender mostly overcame, having little time

indicators.note: mostly says the word for overcame loses its last letter

parts.note: to beat is to overcome
a trice is a very short time

explanation.surface: A champion of a hero mostly won, quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: Hero is the heroine of Much Ado About Nothing, defended by her cousin Beatrice when she is shamed.
explanation.definitionFit: In Much Ado, Beatrice is the cousin who champions the slandered Hero and asks Benedick to fight for her.

clue.text: Main part in Tempest as man searching

indicators.note: part in tells us the answer is a part found inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: The lead role in The Tempest goes to a man searching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the sea, and it also suggests the main part in a play. The answer runs through tempesT AS MAN SEArching.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is an old literary word for the open sea, and this one lies between Australia and New Zealand.

clue.text: Old lieutenant Prince Hal had at first, introduced by Shakespeare

definitions.text: Old lieutenant Prince Hal had at first, introduced by Shakespeare

indicators.note: the four initials follow, being introduced by, the word for Shakespeare

parts.note: Shakespeare is known as the Bard

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A description of an old soldier from Prince Hal's tavern days, brought on stage by Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: Bardolph, the red-nosed drinker, is one of Hal's old companions and a lieutenant in Henry V.
explanation.definitionFit: Bardolph is the Shakespearean rogue who served Prince Hal's circle and ends as a lieutenant hanged for theft in France.

clue.text: Gift of I, thy bard, shown cryptically here?

indicators.note: shown cryptically signals that the letters of the three words are scrambled

parts.note: to be here is to be present

explanation.surface: A gift for the Bard himself, published on his birthday.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared on 23 April, Shakespeare's birthday. 'shown cryptically' rearranges I THY BARD into BIRTHDAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A present given on someone's anniversary of birth is a gift.

clue.text: What 7 suffered concealed by dull arras, perhaps

indicators.note: the crime is concealed by the word for dull around it

parts.note: dry means dull or boring
the heroine of the Bard's poem at 7 down was raped by Tarquin

explanation.surface: An outrage hidden behind a dreary wall hanging.
explanation.walkthrough: An arras is a tapestry hung on a wall, as in Hamlet's Polonius scene.
explanation.definitionFit: An arras is a hanging tapestry, an example of cloth hangings.

clue.text: Bard's poetic subject, girl about Rome, heartless Tarquin's capital

indicators.note: the girl's name goes around the other pieces

parts.note: Lucia is a girl's name

indicators.note: heartless means the middle of Rome is lost, leaving its outer letters
capital means the first letter, the capital letter of Tarquin's

explanation.surface: A girl around Rome is the prize of the cruel Tarquin.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's narrative poem The Rape of Lucrece tells her story.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman matron raped by Tarquin is the heroine of Shakespeare's narrative poem.

clue.text: Leontes' queen, I am turning up on being concealed in this place

indicators.note: the other pieces are concealed in the word for this place

parts.note: here means this place

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up means the letters are written upwards

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am

explanation.surface: A queen is turning up, hiding in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: Leontes' wife in The Winter's Tale hides for sixteen years, so 'concealed' suits the story.
explanation.definitionFit: The wife of Leontes, King of Sicilia, in The Winter's Tale.

clue.text: Shock treatment from Mark Antony initially getting Caesar changing direction

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letters of Mark and Antony
one compass point in the name Caesar is swapped for another, east becoming south

parts.note: taken as written before the swap

explanation.surface: Mark Antony starts treating a shocked Caesar, who changes course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' is a mass of hair, not a jolt: macassar oil was the Victorian hair dressing. E (east) in CAESAR becomes S (south), giving CASSAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Macassar oil was a dressing applied to the hair, so it is a treatment for a shock of hair.

clue.text: One reeling, perhaps, caught in Arden disguised

indicators.note: the letter for caught goes in among the rearranged forest letters
the forest name is disguised by having its letters rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone captured while hiding in the Forest of Arden, as in As You Like It.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disguised' turns ARDEN into DANER, and C goes inside. A reel is a Scottish dance, so a reeler is a dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a lively folk dance, so somebody performing one is a dancer.

clue.text: Adverse criticism given theatre company by American pest

parts.note: a rep is a repertory theatre company
roach is the American short name for a cockroach

explanation.surface: A theatre troupe being slated by an annoying American.
explanation.definitionFit: A reproach is a rebuke or expression of disapproval, which is hostile criticism.

clue.text: National presenting the old pieces to one

parts.note: ye is an old form of the
chess pieces are called men
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone handing out antique pieces to a single person.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Yemen is a national of that country.

clue.text: Actors taking a course for role of Alonso or Ferdinand, say

definitions.text: role of Alonso or Ferdinand, say

parts.note: the actors in a play make up its cast
a way is a course or route

explanation.surface: Performers set off on a route, talking about parts in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: Alonso and Ferdinand are shipwrecked on Prospero's island in The Tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: Both men are washed ashore after the shipwreck in The Tempest, making each a shipwrecked survivor.

clue.text: Disciple's account about wild old Pistol

indicators.note: the account abbreviation goes around the rest
wild signals that the letters are put in an unruly new order

explanation.surface: The tale of a disciple concerning the wild old Pistol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges O and PISTOL into POSTOLI.
explanation.definitionFit: Apostolic means of or relating to the apostles, Christ's followers.

clue.text: Kentish rebel being a scoundrel to English

parts.note: a cad is a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A rebel from Kent is called a rotter by the English.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade led the Kentish revolt of 1450 and appears in Henry VI Part 2; Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Cade led a rising of Kentish men against Henry VI.

clue.text: Feuding family building up castle

indicators.note: building means assembling the letters into a new structure

explanation.surface: A warring clan put up a fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: The Capulets feud with the Montagues in Romeo and Juliet.
explanation.definitionFit: Juliet's family are locked in a vendetta with the Montagues.

clue.text: One of Ford's lines died — get mature new actor?

parts.note: to age is to grow mature
a ham is an overacting actor

explanation.surface: One of Ford's lines dies and a fresh performer must be found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ford' looks like Master Ford of The Merry Wives, but it is the car maker, whose plant at Dagenham in east London made production lines.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ford motor company built cars on its assembly lines at Dagenham.

clue.text: Windsor gentleman making earliest appointment for Falstaff?

definitions.meaning: Master ... is one of the citizens of Windsor in The Merry Wives of Windsor
in Henry IV Part 2 Falstaff recalls being a boy servant to Thomas Mowbray, his first post

explanation.surface: A Windsor man fixes Falstaff's first meeting of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earliest appointment' looks like a diary slot, but it means first job: as a boy, Falstaff served the Duke of Norfolk.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the Windsor husband in the comedy and a boy attendant in a noble household bear this name or title.

clue.text: Cressida's uncle, having sport among animals

indicators.note: the sport goes in among the animals

parts.note: pandas are animals
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: Cressida's uncle takes part in games among the beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: RU is rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: Pandarus is the go-between uncle of Cressida in Troilus and Cressida.

clue.text: Pistol grabbing a king with anger over fine fiddle

indicators.note: the firearm grabs, or holds, the next pieces inside

parts.note: a pistol is a gun
R is for Rex, king

indicators.note: in a down entry over signals the anger word is reversed

parts.note: ire means anger

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's Pistol seizes a king angrily over a fine violin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pistol' looks like Falstaff's crony but is just a gun. 'over' turns IRE into ERI.
explanation.definitionFit: Guarneri violins, made by a family of Cremona luthiers, rank with Stradivari as the finest fiddles.

clue.text: Strange old map — plan showing capital of Navarre

indicators.note: strange signals that the letters are put into an unusual new order

explanation.surface: An odd antique chart whose layout reveals a Spanish regional capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Pamplona is the chief city of the Spanish region of Navarre.

clue.text: Former European, Louis of France?

parts.note: past means former
Eur is an abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: An ex-European, a French king called Louis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Louis of France' suggests a king, but it is Louis Pasteur the scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur was the French chemist behind pasteurisation.

clue.text: Like the rest of the crowned heads, according to Henry IV

definitions.text: Like the rest of the crowned heads, according to Henry IV

parts.words: Like the rest of the crowned heads, according to Henry IV
parts.note: the king's line in Henry IV Part 2 says the head that wears a crown lies without comfort, so a monarch's repose is troubled

explanation.walkthrough: 'the rest' looks like 'the others', but it means repose: the head that wears a crown lies restlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: The quoted line describes how anxious and troubled a king's sleep is.

clue.text: New actor, odd terms — everything included in embryonic part

annotationWithheld.why: New actor, odd terms - everything included in embryonic part (8): no parse of 'New actor, odd terms' and 'everything included' gives the letters of ECTODERM (there is no A or S in it); scan matches and searches find no source
annotationWithheld.clue: New actor, odd terms — everything included in embryonic part

clue.text: Speeches heard again in city gardens?

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London
to hoe is to work a garden, so one who gardens hoes

explanation.surface: Talks repeated in urban parks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gardens' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Echoes are sounds, including spoken words, returned and heard once more.

clue.text: One may project negative views involving Regan and Lear, but not Cordelia, ultimately

indicators.note: involving in its sense of entangling or rolling together signals the names are jumbled
but not tells us to take away a letter from the mixed names
ultimately asks for the final letter of the youngest daughter's name

explanation.surface: Someone with gloomy opinions about Regan and Lear but not, in the end, Cordelia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negative views' reads as gloomy opinions, but the definition is a photographic negative. 'involving' mixes REGAN and LEAR, and 'but not' removes A, the last letter of Cordelia.
explanation.definitionFit: A photographic enlarger shines light through a negative to project a bigger image onto paper.

clue.text: County played, slaughtered at Tewkesbury

definitions.meaning: the Duke of this title is a character in Henry VI Part 3, killed after the battle of Tewkesbury

explanation.surface: A county side played, and was massacred at Tewkesbury.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a county cricket match; Tewkesbury is a town in Gloucestershire.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both an English shire and the title of Edmund Beaufort, the Lancastrian duke executed after Tewkesbury.

clue.text: Shakespearean lieutenant, one with "a lean and hungry look" has nothing for us

indicators.note: the clue says the conspirator's name has one thing put in place of another
the clue says the conspirator's name has one thing put in place of another

parts.words: one with "a lean and hungry look"
parts.note: Caesar describes Cassius as having a lean and hungry look in Julius Caesar
taken as written
O is the figure nought, nothing

explanation.surface: A hungry-looking officer takes nothing for us.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the US at the end of CASSIUS for O. Cassio is Othello's lieutenant.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Cassio is Othello's lieutenant in the tragedy.
